newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DOLLAR/MARK DRIVEN BY CROSSES IN SINGAPORE.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR/MARK DRIVEN BY CROSSES IN SINGAPORE.

text.p: The U.S. dollar looked slightly offered against the mark on Wednesday with activity driven largely by the mark/yen and sterling/mark cross, Singapore dealers said.
"Some stop-loss buy orders were triggered in mark/yen at 62.50 this morning, so it's holding very well. But I'm sure there are sell orders at 62.70/80," a European bank dealer said.
He said the dollar was unlikely to stray out of a 1.8580-1.8700 marks range ahead of the release of U.S. retail sales and wholesale inflation data for July due at 1230 GMT.
Economists surveyed by Reuters expected retail sales data to show a rise of 0.7 percent in July after rising 0.5 percent in June.
Both the overall and core Producer Price Index were expected to have risen by 0.1 percent in July.
"Even if the dollar breaks 1.8580 marks, I wouldn't get too bearish. Based on the last two days, I don't think New York wants to bring the dollar down," the dealer said.
He said longer term players would see any downward moves as an opportunity to go long. "Maybe they think 1.89 marks will be revisited or 1.90 in the coming months," he said.
Dealers said the dollar was showing a bid tone against the yen but Japanese exporter offers near the 117 yen level would continue to block further rises.
